planting.note: Plant own-root cutting-grown stock in spring in full sun to partial shade on well-drained soil.

directions: Silver Spire is a narrow, upright English yew introduced by Treseders Nursery in Cornwall, UK, in the late 1980s, grown for an unusual seasonal color sequence rather than its tight fastigiate form alone. New growth opens a cheerful yellow, fades to pale yellow and creamy white at the leaf margins through summer, then surprises with a silvery cast once cold weather arrives. It is propagated from rooted cuttings on its own roots and grows mostly upward with little lateral spread, making it a space-efficient vertical accent. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, as with other English yew selections.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun to light shade on cool, evenly moist, well-drained soil.

directions: Green Globe is a semi-dwarf, multi-stemmed subalpine fir selected for its refined texture, with short, soft, lustrous needles that point forward along the branches rather than radiating outward like the species. New growth emerges bright green in spring and often takes on bluish tones as it matures through the season. Its dense, rounded habit and manageable size make it more practical for garden use than typical subalpine fir, which is usually too large and site-specific for small landscapes. Give it full sun to light shade and cool, evenly moist, well-drained soil similar to its high-elevation native range.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on average, well-drained soil.

directions: Acro-yellow is a golden-foliaged sport in the 'Acrocona' group of Norway spruce, grown as much for its ornamental cones as for its needle color. A profusion of raspberry-red cones emerges at the branch tips each spring, standing out sharply against the bright yellow foliage before fading to light brown as the cones mature and the foliage settles to a softer, frosted yellow. Like other Acrocona-type spruces it tends toward a broad, semi-weeping habit rather than a strict pyramid. Full sun brings out the best cone and foliage color, and it should be planted in average, well-drained soil.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Morris Blue is a narrow, pyramidal Korean pine selection that originated at the Morris Arboretum of the University of Pennsylvania, chosen for a striking mix of silvery-blue and bluish-green needles that catch the light along thick, slightly curved foliage. Large, plump cones in a matching bluish-green add further seasonal interest before they mature. As an intermediate-growth-rate selection it builds a substantial, well-proportioned specimen faster than many dwarf pines while staying narrower than the species. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil, as is typical for Korean pine.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Taylor's Sunburst is an upright, narrow lodgepole pine selected for an especially dramatic spring display, pushing brilliant lemon-yellow new growth that contrasts sharply against needles from the previous season that have already matured to green. Small, bright red pollen cones appear at the same time, adding another layer of color to the spring show. Outside of that seasonal flush the tree settles into a fairly typical narrow pine silhouette. It wants full sun and well-drained soil, and like other lodgepole pine selections is usually grown grafted onto Scots pine rootstock.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on sharply drained soil.

directions: Paul's Dwarf is a fine-textured mugo pine selection notable for exceptionally short, medium-green needles arranged perpendicular to the stem, giving the branches a distinctive skeletal, almost bottlebrush look rather than the dense tufting typical of most mugo cultivars. Its small, compact scale suits rock gardens and trough plantings better than larger landscape mugo selections. Like other mugo pines, it prefers a sunny, sharply drained site and resents wet, heavy soil. Minimal pruning is needed given its naturally restrained growth rate.

common_name: Shirome Janome Variegated Japanese Black Pine

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; tolerates wind and salt spray.

directions: Shirome Janome is a vigorous Japanese black pine selection grown for its bold, banded needle variegation, with long, dark green needles marked by distinct golden-yellow rings that make it stand out sharply at a distance. Its strong growth rate and substantial eventual size suit it to use as a specimen or focal point rather than a small-space planting. Like other Japanese black pines it tolerates wind, salt spray, and poor sandy soils better than most ornamental conifers, provided it has full sun and good drainage. Needle variegation tends to be most pronounced on vigorous new growth each year.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Meyer's Dwarf is a compact selection of Greek fir prized for glossy, dark green foliage and notably better vigor and drought tolerance than many other dwarf fir cultivars. It builds a broad, rounded form that stays wider than tall, reaching roughly three feet high and four and a half feet wide after a decade. Full sun and well-drained soil keep it healthiest, and its above-average heat and drought tolerance make it a more forgiving choice than most firs for gardeners outside cool, moist climates.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on sharply drained soil.

directions: Katere is a spreading dwarf cedar of Lebanon with soft, long gray-green needles on a low, mounding frame that stays well under a foot tall even after a decade, reaching only about eight to twelve inches high and twelve to eighteen inches wide. Its small scale makes it a natural fit for rockeries, troughs, and compact gardens where a standard Lebanon cedar would be far too large. Plant in full sun with sharply drained soil, and expect slow, steady growth that rarely needs any corrective pruning.

common_name: Filip's Golden Tears Weeping Lawson Cypress

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Filip's Golden Tears is a strictly weeping, needle-narrow Lawson cypress whose gold-variegated foliage reads almost like a vertical exclamation point in the landscape. It can reach twelve to fifteen feet tall while staying only a couple of feet wide, which makes it useful as a dramatic narrow accent in tight spaces where a broader golden conifer would not fit. Full sun develops the strongest gold color, and it needs consistently well-drained soil, since Lawson cypress in general performs poorly in wet or compacted ground. Little to no pruning is required to maintain its naturally cascading form.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on evenly moist, well-drained soil.

directions: Lemonade is a vigorous, tree-form Norway spruce from Bob Fincham's well-known Golden Seedling breeding line, carrying bright golden foliage on graceful pendant branches rather than the stiffer habit of many golden conifers. Its fast growth and eventual size, roughly twelve to fifteen feet tall and about two-thirds as wide after a decade, make it better suited to a specimen role than a small garden bed. Full sun develops the strongest gold color, and even moisture with good drainage keeps growth steady. It combines the ornamental interest of golden foliage with the reliability and hardiness of standard Norway spruce.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun to light shade on evenly moist, well-drained soil.

directions: Ferny Creek Prostrate is a perfectly flat, ground-hugging selection of Caucasian spruce, holding short, glossy, dark green needles on a spreading mat that stays close to the soil rather than mounding upward. After ten years it typically reaches only about a foot tall while spreading some three feet wide, making it a useful low, textural groundcover for a conifer bed or rock garden edge. Give it full sun to light shade and evenly moist, well-drained soil, consistent with Caucasian spruce in general.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; reserve a permanent spot given its glacial growth.

directions: Blue Pearl is a true miniature Colorado spruce, a witch's-broom selection from Iseli Nursery that keeps the species' prickly, sky-blue needles on a tight, cushion-shaped dwarf frame. After a decade it typically measures only about six inches tall and a foot wide, making it a favorite for trough gardens and miniature conifer collections rather than open landscape use. Full sun keeps its blue coloration most intense, and it should be planted in well-drained soil and left largely unpruned given its glacial growth rate.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun to light shade on average, well-drained soil.

directions: Primo is an Iseli Nursery selection of eastern arborvitae bred to look more like a Hinoki cypress than a typical arborvitae, with refined, scale-like foliage that twists and turns along the branches for extra texture. It holds a vivid green through the growing season before muting somewhat over winter. Growth is slow and even, at only two to four inches a year, so it keeps a tidy, upright form without shearing for a long time. Plant in full sun to light shade in average, well-drained soil, as with other arborvitae selections.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock on disease-resistant rootstock in spring in full sun on sharply drained soil.

directions: Blue Surprise is a fine-textured Lawson cypress selection whose juvenile, upward-pointing foliage stays soft to the touch despite its prickly appearance. Steel-blue needles are highlighted with silver through the growing season and take on a purplish cast in winter cold, giving noticeable seasonal color change. It is now typically supplied on disease-resistant rootstock, addressing root rot susceptibility that has historically limited Lawson cypress in wetter gardens. Expect a narrowly pyramidal habit reaching roughly six feet tall by two feet wide after a decade, growing best in full sun with sharp drainage.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Ruby Teardrops is a globose Colorado spruce selected for a striking spring display, when fresh teal-blue foliage emerges alongside clusters of magenta seed cones that dangle from the branch tips like ornaments. Outside of that seasonal show it holds the dense, rounded habit typical of globose Colorado spruce cultivars. Full sun brings out the best cone and needle color, and it should be grown in well-drained soil typical of Colorado spruce selections in general. Its compact, rounded form fits well in a mixed conifer bed without the size demands of full-sized blue spruce.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on average, well-drained soil.

directions: Jantar is a narrow, upright arborvitae raised from seed of the widely planted 'Smaragd' in Poland, carrying golden foliage that deepens to rich amber tones through winter rather than fading or bronzing poorly as some gold arborvitae cultivars do. Its columnar habit makes it useful for screening or vertical accents in a smaller footprint than standard green arborvitae. Plant in full sun for the best gold color, in average, well-drained soil, and expect the kind of reliable, weather-tolerant performance that has made 'Smaragd'-type arborvitae popular landscape plants.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; tolerates urban conditions.

directions: Herman, also sold under the trade name Prairie Statesman, is an extremely hardy and drought-resistant Swiss stone pine selection suited to harsh prairie and urban conditions as readily as a traditional garden. Its narrow form is held together by a strong central leader and lateral branches that curve upward and inward, a structure that sheds heavy snow loads well rather than splaying open under weight. The combination of toughness and a neat, upright silhouette gives it an elegant, almost formal presence despite its rugged constitution. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil; it tolerates urban stresses and wind better than most ornamental pines.

common_name: Tanima no Yuki Variegated Japanese White Pine

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring with afternoon shade protection in hot climates, on well-drained soil.

directions: Tanima no Yuki, Japanese for 'snow of the valley,' is a Japanese white pine selection grown for new growth that elongates in shifting shades of pink, cream, and green before the curved needles unfurl into a flocked, snow-dusted appearance. That variegation is striking but also delicate, since intense summer sun can scorch the lightened needle tissue. High, dappled, or afternoon shade protects the color in hot climates, while cooler regions can grow it in fuller sun. Give it well-drained soil and treat it as a specimen where its unusual coloring can be appreciated up close.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on consistently moist soil until established.

directions: Schirrmann's Nordlicht is a witch's-broom selection found on the dawn redwood cultivar 'White Spot' by German grower Winfried Schirrmann, and it carries the same cheerful bright foliage while growing far more slowly and compactly than a seed-grown dawn redwood, settling into a globular rather than pyramidal shape. After a decade it typically reaches five to six feet tall and three to five feet wide. It needs regular watering while becoming established, after which it tolerates drier conditions noticeably better, and like other dawn redwoods it also handles wet, seasonally flooded soil without trouble. Plant in full sun for the best growth and form.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Wiethorst is a dwarf, narrowly pyramidal selection of the naturally occurring hybrid between eastern white pine and Himalayan white pine, first discovered near Berlin in 1905. It combines the long, graceful needles of its Himalayan parent with the superior cold hardiness inherited from eastern white pine, giving it a softer, more pendulous texture than most hardy pines. Its compact, dwarf habit keeps it in scale with smaller gardens where either full-sized parent species would be too large. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil typical of five-needle pines.

common_name: Gold Drift Weeping Golden Norway Spruce

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on average, well-drained soil; stake a leader for height.

directions: Gold Drift is a golden sport of the weeping Norway spruce cultivar 'Reflexa', discovered by Bob Fincham of Coenosium Gardens in Washington state. New growth opens lime green in early spring and deepens to a vibrant gold through late spring and summer sun, holding color into winter before fading toward a more subdued tone as the season progresses. Like its weeping parent it builds a broad, cascading, irregular form rather than an upright spire, so it benefits from staking if more height is wanted. Full sun develops the richest gold color, and it should be grown in average, well-drained soil.

common_name: Little Leo Miniature Taiwan Coffin Fir

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun to light shade on well-drained soil.

directions: Little Leo is a true miniature selection of Taiwan coffin fir, forming a flattened, ground-hugging pincushion of foliage rather than the tall forest tree typical of the species. Its tiny scale and tight form make it a specialty piece for miniature conifer collections and trough gardens rather than general landscape use. Notably, it performs well under hot, humid growing conditions that many other dwarf conifers find stressful, making it useful in warmer regions. Plant in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil and expect extremely slow growth with little need for maintenance.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring with afternoon shade protection, on moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.

directions: Picola is a dwarf, pyramidal selection of Japanese umbrella pine, keeping the species' distinctive whorled rings of thick, glossy needles on a scaled-down frame that reaches only about two feet tall and a foot and a half wide after a decade. That slow, compact growth makes it far more practical for smaller gardens than the species, which can eventually become a substantial tree. Give it evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and some protection from the harshest afternoon sun, conditions that suit umbrella pine in general. Its neat pyramidal shape needs no pruning to maintain.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on sharply drained soil.

directions: Kenwith is a small selection of Cypriot cedar, a naturally diminutive cedar species, combining notably tiny needles with an upright, tree-like habit in miniature rather than the sprawling or prostrate form seen in many dwarf conifer selections. Its compact scale makes a full cedar silhouette achievable in a modest garden footprint. Plant in full sun with sharply drained soil, since Cypriot cedar, like its Lebanon and Atlas relatives, is intolerant of wet feet. Growth is slow and steady, keeping the plant naturally tidy with little pruning needed.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun to partial shade on average, well-drained soil.

directions: Wichtel is a true miniature Norway spruce, a witch's-broom selection found in the United Kingdom on the cultivar 'Humilis', and it grows at a glacial pace of only a fraction of an inch per year. That scale places it among the smallest Norway spruce cultivars grown, making it a specialty plant for trough gardens and miniature conifer collections rather than general landscape use. Plant in full sun to partial shade in average, well-drained soil, and expect it to remain a tight, dense little mound for decades with essentially no pruning required.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun on sharply drained soil.

directions: Bergman is a compact Japanese white pine selection with soft, silvery-blue needles that carry a slight twist, giving the foliage extra textural interest compared to straighter-needled pine cultivars. Its tidy, slow-building habit suits smaller gardens and conifer collections better than the larger forms of the species typically grown as landscape trees. It is cold hardy to USDA zone 4 and, like other Japanese white pine selections, performs best in full sun with sharply drained soil. Minimal pruning is needed to keep its naturally compact form.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on moist, well-drained soil; train or stake while young.

directions: Puli is a weeping European larch selection that produces light green, lacy foliage cascading in distinct curtains down a slope or over rocks, an effect that depends heavily on staking height and training in its early years. Each fall that curtain turns a vivid golden yellow before the needles drop, echoing the species' deciduous seasonal display in a more sculptural form. It is quite cold hardy and adaptable, but needs a sunny site and reliably moist, well-drained soil to thrive, as with European larch generally. Given its trainable, cascading habit, it works well draped over a wall or large rock feature as a living waterfall.

common_name: Niagara Falls Weeping Eastern White Pine

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained, slightly acidic soil; train or stake while young.

directions: Niagara Falls is a weeping eastern white pine selection with a dense, full branch structure that, true to its name, can be trained to cascade downward in sheets when staked, or allowed to spread and mound when left untrained. Its soft, blue-green needles and billowing habit give it a softer appearance than most weeping conifers, which tend toward a sparser, more linear look. Final size and shape depend heavily on how it is staked and trained in its early years. Plant in full sun in well-drained, slightly acidic soil typical of eastern white pine.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; stake a leader early for height.

directions: The Blues is a weeping Colorado spruce selection with powdery blue needles and a strongly horizontal, mounding growth habit; left unstaked it sprawls along the ground rather than gaining height. Staking a leader when the plant is young is the standard way growers coax it into a more upright, cascading specimen form, after which it typically reaches around six feet tall and four feet wide in a decade. Its intense blue color holds up well through the growing season in full sun. Plant in well-drained soil, as with other Colorado spruce cultivars, and expect excellent cold hardiness.

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun to light shade on well-drained soil.

directions: Pendula Bruns is a narrow, strictly weeping Serbian spruce introduced by Bruns Nursery in Germany in 1955, carrying the species' distinctive bi-colored needles, dark green above and silvery beneath, on dense, drooping branches with upward-curving tips. In spring it adds a profusion of pendant violet-purple cones that provide extra seasonal interest beyond its elegant silhouette. After a decade it typically reaches ten to twelve feet tall while staying a slender four to five feet wide, making it a graceful vertical anchor without taking up much ground space. Grow it in full sun to light shade in well-drained soil.

common_name: Tom Thumb Gold Miniature Golden Caucasian Spruce

planting.note: Plant grafted stock in spring in full sun on well-drained soil.

directions: Tom Thumb Gold is a miniature golden-needled Caucasian spruce that arose as a baseball-sized witch's broom found on Picea orientalis 'Skylands'. It forms a dense, low mound of radiating tiny twigs bearing numerous short, bright golden-yellow needles concentrated at the shoot tips, distinguishing it from the plain-green miniature 'Tom Thumb' selection of the same species. Full sun develops the strongest gold color, and it should be grown in well-drained soil typical of Caucasian spruce. Its very slow growth rate suits it well to rock gardens and miniature conifer collections.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full sun to light shade on moist, well-drained soil.

directions: Pixie Dust is a dwarf form of the already-dwarf Alberta spruce, selected for striking yellow new growth that contrasts sharply against the deep green of its mature foliage each season. That two-toned flush gives an otherwise classic conical dwarf spruce extra seasonal interest without changing its tidy, dense habit. It stays notably smaller than the familiar 'Conica' selection most gardeners know, making it a better fit for very small beds and containers. Plant in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained soil, and watch for spider mites in hot, dry conditions, a common issue for Alberta spruce selections generally.
